sections.heading: Repair or Replace Your Water Heater?
sections.body: Start with the symptoms, not just the age of the unit. Tell us whether you have no hot water, fluctuating temperature, noise or visible moisture. We assess the equipment and explain whether a repair is practical or replacement is the better option. A leaking tank may require replacement; a leak at a connection can call for a different repair.

sections.heading: Planning a Water Heater Replacement
sections.body: The right replacement depends on household hot-water use, available space and the existing gas or electrical setup. We discuss tank and tankless options and assess the connections and installation requirements for your home before quoting the work. Share the model information and photos of the existing unit when requesting an estimate.

faqs.q: Do You Repair Gas and Electric Water Heaters?
faqs.a: Yes. We repair and replace gas and electric tank water heaters and install tankless systems. Include your water heater type and the symptoms in your service request so we can discuss the next step.

faqs.q: Should I Switch to a Tankless Water Heater?
faqs.a: That depends on your hot-water needs and the installation work involved. We assess the existing setup, including gas line sizing where applicable, and explain the options before recommending a conversion.

faqs.q: How Much Does Water Heater Replacement Cost?
faqs.a: The estimate depends on the equipment, access and changes needed for the installation. We provide free estimates with no service-call fee and review the proposed work and pricing with you.

faqs.q: Can I Get Help With No Hot Water After Hours?
faqs.a: Emergency service is available 24/7 by call or text at 314-220-1827. Contact the team for current availability and arrival timing. An online request does not guarantee immediate dispatch.

sections.heading: Tell Us Where You Notice the Problem
sections.body: A leak may be obvious under a sink or show up as a stain away from the pipe. Tell us when you first noticed it, whether it happens continuously or only when a fixture runs, and which areas are affected. Photos of visible moisture and nearby plumbing can help the team understand the problem before the visit.

sections.heading: A Targeted Repair or a Larger Replacement?
sections.body: A failed fitting or valve may need a focused repair. Recurring leaks or deteriorated pipe can warrant a discussion about replacing a section of line. We assess the affected plumbing, explain the proposed scope and review pricing before you decide how to proceed.

faqs.q: Can You Repair a Leaking Shutoff Valve?
faqs.a: Yes. Shutoff valves, supply lines and leaking fittings are part of our plumbing repair work. Tell us which fixture the valve serves and whether the leak is active when you contact us.

faqs.q: Do You Repair Both Supply and Drain Lines?
faqs.a: Yes. We handle supply line and drain line leaks. Let us know whether water appears continuously or only when you use a sink, shower, toilet or appliance.

faqs.q: Does a Leak Mean My Whole House Needs Repiping?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The source of the leak and the condition of the surrounding plumbing determine the options. We explain whether a local repair, section replacement or broader work makes sense for the problem we find.

faqs.q: How Do I Request Help With an Active Leak?
faqs.a: Call or text 314-220-1827 for an active leak or after-hours emergency. Emergency service is available 24/7; the team confirms availability and arrival timing. For a routine repair, you can also submit a website service request.

detail.heading: Toilet and Faucet Repair and Replacement

sections.heading: Fix the Problem or Update the Fixture
sections.body: A worn internal part can sometimes be repaired without replacing the whole fixture. If you want a different toilet or faucet, we can discuss replacement instead. Tell us about running water, drips, loose fixtures or reduced flow, as well as any changes you want to make.

sections.heading: Plan the Replacement Before You Buy
sections.body: Fixture fit and existing connections matter. For a toilet, share the model you are considering and photos of the existing installation. For a faucet, include the sink or countertop mounting arrangement and connections below it. Contact us before buying if you want to discuss the installation scope and what information we need.

faqs.q: Can a Running Toilet Be Repaired?
faqs.a: A running toilet does not automatically need replacement. We assess the tank components and explain the repair options. If you prefer a new fixture, we can also discuss replacement.

faqs.q: Do You Replace Kitchen and Bathroom Faucets?
faqs.a: Yes. We repair and replace kitchen and bathroom faucets. Tell us where the fixture is installed, what is wrong with it and whether you already have a replacement in mind.

faqs.q: Can I Supply My Own Toilet or Faucet?
faqs.a: Contact us with the model information before purchasing or scheduling. We can discuss compatibility, the installation scope and any additional parts that may be needed for your existing plumbing.

faqs.q: Is There a Charge for a Replacement Estimate?
faqs.a: Estimates are free, and there is no service-call fee. The proposed price depends on the fixture and installation work. We review the scope and pricing with you before work begins.
